title: Increase of Magnetic Trap Loading Efficiency for $^{39}\mathrm{K}$ Bose--Einstein Condensation Experiments
authors: Yihao Cheng, Xiaoyang Shen, Weixin Li, Hao Du, Hongwu Zhao, Lin Xia
abstract: During the experimental sequence, a large atom number is important for the creation of high-quality Bose--Einstein condensates. We report an experimental increase of about 15% in magnetic-trap (MT) loading efficiency by optimizing the MT loading process. The loading time is much shorter than the lifetime of the atoms in the MT, which means atom loss during loading due to the finite trap lifetime can be neglected. We obtain an almost pure $^{39}\mathrm{K}$ condensate with $1.2\times10^{5}$ atoms after evaporative cooling in our optical trap.
summary: This paper reports experimental improvements in loading efficiency for $^{39}\mathrm{K}$ atoms into a magnetic trap, achieving a 15% increase by optimizing the loading current and sequence. By maximizing the initial atom number, the authors successfully created a high-quality Bose-Einstein Condensate, establishing better conditions for subsequent quantum gas research.
main_problem: The primary goal was to achieve the stable production of high-quality Bose-Einstein Condensates (BEC) for $^{39}\mathrm{K}$ atoms, which necessitates maximizing the initial atom number loaded into the trap.
main_result: The authors successfully increased the magnetic trap loading efficiency by approximately 15% through optimization of the loading sequence, resulting in a pure $^{39}\mathrm{K}$ condensate with $1.2	imes10^{5}$ atoms.
method: The optimization involved systematically varying the magnetic trap loading current ($I_{	ext{MT}}$) and implementing a specific three-step loading sequence.
model_or_system: The experiment uses $^{39}\mathrm{K}$ ultracold atoms trapped sequentially in a Magneto-Optical Trap (MOT), a magnetic trap (MT), and finally cooled in an optical dipole trap.
key_observables: Loaded atom number (measured after free expansion), BEC atom number ($1.2	imes10^{5}$ atoms), and atom decay rates over time.
important_parameters: Optimized MT current range ($26 	ext{ A}$ to $35 	ext{ A}$), initial magnetic field gradient ($\approx 1.23 	ext{ G} \cdot 	ext{cm}^{-1} \cdot 	ext{A}^{-1}$), and trap lifetime ($	ext{1/e}$ lifetime of $29.8 	ext{ s}$).
main_assumptions: The atom loss during the loading process due to the finite trap lifetime was found to be negligible compared to the loading time.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the initial MT loading state, the optimized three-step loading sequence, the dependence of loaded atom number on $I_{	ext{MT}}$ (showing the 15% improvement), and the BEC transition during evaporative cooling.
paper_structure: The paper details the necessity of high atom numbers, presents the optimization of the MT loading process using a specific current ramping sequence, reports the resulting increase in loading efficiency, and concludes with the successful observation of the BEC.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial experimental data on optimizing the initial loading stage for ultracold atomic gases, which is a fundamental prerequisite for studying complex many-body physics in BECs.

One is that the atomic cloud has a high optical depth after the GM stage.
